title: Power sliding doors sticking, stopping partway, or dead
symptoms: Door stops partway, motor runs but the door doesn't move, door won't latch, or no response at all.
cause: Low 12 V battery voltage, dry runners, a worn cable sheath binding in the pulleys, a broken cable, or a failed motor.
fix: Battery and fuses first, then a reset and lubrication. Replace the cable or motor if those don't fix it.

title: CVT judder or shudder when pulling away
symptoms: Shudder or vibration at low speed under light throttle, sometimes a whine.
cause: Worn or never-changed CVT fluid. Toyota lists no change interval, so many imports arrive on original fluid at 100,000+ km.
fix: Japanese garages report judder curing after a fluid change (often a full machine exchange). Do it with the right fluid (CVT TC/FE) and a proper level check.

title: Knocking from the rear over bumps
symptoms: Clunk or knock from the back on uneven roads.
cause: UK buying guides point to the rear axle (torsion beam) mounting bushes.
fix: Inspect the bushes and replace any that are worn.

title: Front knock or rattle over small bumps
symptoms: Light knocking from the front, often on broken road surfaces.
cause: Worn anti-roll bar drop links or bar bushes, common on heavy MPVs.
fix: Replace the drop links and D-bushes (part numbers in Parts).

title: 2AZ-FE oil consumption
symptoms: Oil level drops between changes with no leak; bluish smoke on start-up or after engine braking. Bad cases use 1 L per 1,000–3,000 km.
cause: Oil getting past the piston rings (carboned-up rings, blocked oil return holes). Japanese sources say engines built roughly 2005–2014 are affected, especially early ones. Toyota Japan ran a warranty extension (not a recall): 9 years from first registration, unlimited mileage, covering ECU reprogramming, new pistons/rings/oil jets or a short block. Almost every 20 series is now outside that.
fix: Check the dipstick monthly. A Japanese article says dealer-repaired engines often show black sealant (grey suggests original), but that's not conclusive. Ask for warranty-repair records on a Japanese history report. A proper fix is new pistons/rings or a replacement engine. Additives and flushes are a gamble.

title: 2AZ-FE head bolt threads pulling out of the block
symptoms: Coolant loss and overheating, like a head gasket failure.
cause: Stripped head bolt threads in the aluminium block, usually the rear bolts. Mainly affects earlier blocks; not confirmed whether 2008+ ANH20 engines are affected.
fix: Thread inserts (e.g. Time-Sert) or a replacement block.

title: Hard-to-reach rear spark plugs (V6)
symptoms: Not a fault, but a known labour cost.
cause: The rear bank sits under the intake plenum.
fix: Budget for the plenum to come off. Do all six plugs at once.

title: Only FM 76–90 MHz on the radio
symptoms: Can't tune UK FM stations (88–108 MHz).
fix: Fit a band expander, or replace the head unit. Many importers fit an expander before sale; check it works.

title: Coolant leak from the water pump
symptoms: Pink crusty residue around the pump, falling coolant level, sweet smell, sometimes bearing noise.
cause: Water pump seal wear, typically around 80,000–120,000 km.
fix: Replace the pump (and the drive belt while you're there). A Japanese garage logged about 3 hours' labour for the 2AZ.

title: Oil leaks: cam cover and timing chain tensioner
symptoms: Oily residue on the cam cover edges and the front of the engine.
cause: Hardened cam cover gasket; tensioner gasket weeping.
fix: New cam cover gasket (clean the faces and use sealant at the joints, torque to spec, don't overtighten) and a new tensioner gasket.

title: Torn boots: drop links and lower ball joints
symptoms: Grease flung around the front suspension; knocking once they wear.
cause: Perished rubber boots, common on 10+ year-old cars. Spotted at a Japanese 106,500 km shaken.
fix: Replace the drop links, and the lower ball joints if their boots have split (the boots usually aren't sold separately).

title: Pearl white (070) paint peeling
symptoms: Clear coat or paint lifting and blistering on the roof, pillars, wing and tailgate edges.
cause: Poor paint adhesion made worse by UV and heat. Widely reported on 070 White Pearl.
fix: Repaint the affected panels. Any Toyota Japan goodwill has long expired. Check carefully when buying a white car.

title: Rear air-con weak or losing gas
symptoms: Front A/C cold, rear blowing warm; needs regassing often.
cause: Leaking rear evaporator or corroded rear pipes.
fix: Leak test with UV dye. The rear evaporator needs interior trim stripped, so it's a big job.

title: Floaty ride, bouncing after bumps
symptoms: Keeps bouncing after bumps; oil misting on the shock bodies.
cause: Worn shock absorbers, a heavy van on 100,000+ km.
fix: Replace the shocks in pairs (KYB do OE-type units).
